steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Who are you?!
I told you not to turn around. You let the mark get away.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I said, who the hell are you?!
Easy now, my dear Graf. Settle down.
My official identity can be a bit messy to explain, so just treat me as a spy. I am called Biegler.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You... Why'd you have to jump out this exact moment? That man escaped because of YOU!

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: Considering he ended up down in the sewers, it'll take him a long time to find another exit.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: Besides, you stopped him before he went into the sewer. Who knows, maybe the two of you saw that you were in a disadvantageous position and tried to put on a little show to try to fool me.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You seriously think we're in cahoots? He and I?!

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: Or are you going to tell me that someone coerced you into going to see Gertrude? Spare me the bad jokes.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: You're worth much more than he is, Graf Urtica.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You can't stop me.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: When it comes to combat ability, it is true that I can't stop you. But think carefully.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: This is a job straight from Their Majesties. Take a look.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I've dealt with these things since I was six.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: I personally don't mind your snark, but you'd best show some self-restraint when it comes to Their Majesties' affairs.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Restraint? When you, a lowly spy, figure out that you've got the wrong person, you're going to be the one begging for forgiveness.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: You don't seem to understand the situation you're in, my good Graf Urtica.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: But enough of that. Don't try to stall for time here. Come with me.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Where to?

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: To where you belong. Don't worry, we've prepared detention facilities for suspects from all walks of life. I assure you, you'll enjoy the finest treatment.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Let me tell you something, Herr Biegler.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: Ready to beg for mercy? Or is it a bribe? In case of the latter, I'd be more than glad to oblige.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I doubt a little bit of money is enough for you to let me go. Why do I get the impression that you'd take me away regardless, even after you pocketed the money?

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: Clever boy.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I find you rather easy to get along with, Herr Biegler. You remind me of the Urtica I know so well, where most of the people are just as 'upstanding' as you.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: I am honored to hear that.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: But what I really want to know is what that man is doing in the sewers.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: But you were the one who stopped him, right under my nose.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Well, this is a bit embarrassing to say, but I wanted to resolve things up here.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: One of my agents liked to tell stories that would make you want to hurl. Of the ones that instantly killed your appetite for the day, the worst all came from the sewers.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: Ah. If your stomach is upset, perhaps we should go for a cup of coffee to smooth things over.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I'd love to, but I'd much rather find out what he's doing down there. I might as well go after him.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: And this is all your fault, Herr Biegler.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: As long as you let me head down, you can keep pointing your wand at me. I won't try to run.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: I will warn you in advance—There will be consequences for running away from me without authorization, regardless of the reason.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: What kind? Will you put me down?

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: You'd at least be stripped of your status. Even if you're proven innocent in the future, you'd never be able to step into the Spire of Urtica ever again.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Don't threaten me with a good time. I might be even more inclined to try running now.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: (Shakes head)

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: In any case, since you insist on heading down there... After you, Graf Urtica.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: I'll be keeping a close eye on you.

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: Hibiscus, this isn't a lecture, but y'can't speak to Mein Herr that way.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: But, Mr. Czerny is...

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: There's lots of things he can't say, leavin' this old lady to say 'em.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Please come in.

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: Do you know how the Afterglow got its name?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I don't.

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: Mein Herr once said...

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: 'It is precisely because night falls, that the afterglow is even more precious. If the long veil of night were to never lift, what could be more dazzling and awe-inspiring than the warm afterglow?'

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: It's a wonderful saying, but...

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: Oh, the two over there are–– Frau Ursula, and Hibiscus?

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: Come, come! If you want to chat, do it over here!

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: Why the long face, Hibiscus? Did something happen?

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: If you're worried that my food isn't healthy enough, I also have sparkling water here. Come, come!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: We're still––

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: Let's oblige him this time.

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: Frau Ursula, what's wrong with Hibiscus? Did she get into an argument?

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: No, none of that. Enough random guessing.

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: I was telling Hibiscus about the history of the Afterglow.

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: The Afterglow's history? Now that's something I couldn't be more familiar with.

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: Not bragging either. But I bet I know even more than Frau Ursula here.

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: The Afterglow didn't used to be a residential area for the Infected. It was one of Vyseheim's industrial plates.

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: Don't underestimate me just because I'm setting up shop over here. Back in the day, I was in charge of feeding hundreds of associates.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Industry... Could it be that this place was turned into an Infected residential area because of the spread of Oripathy due to industrial waste?

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: Industrialization did bring a lot of Infected here, but back in Leithanien's old days, there was no such thing as a ghetto for Infected... Hah, I won't keep rambling on.

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: One year, Vyseheim constructed a magnificent concert hall that shocked the world with but a single order from Him, His Majesty... known now as our Afterglow Hall. Back then, that's not what the concert hall was called.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: His Majesty? Which one are you referring to?

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: Oh dear, Hibiscus, let's not worry about the details, alright?

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: If it's 'His' Majesty...

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: ...I get it.

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: When the concert hall was completed, 'He' still reigned, and nobody dared to say anything.

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: But He left us just as quickly, and Graf Strollo, who took over Vyseheim, hated this concert hall.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Maybe hate isn't the right word, but rather... was too quick to show loyalty?

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: Shh–– No random guessing.

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: A few years later, the powers issued an order to supposedly improve the treatment of the Infected. The Graf at that time took the opportunity to lump the concert hall together with the industrial plate, and turned it all into the Infected ghetto.

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: I looked all over and before that, there were no such things as 'Infected quarters' anywhere in Leithanien.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: The Count, the Graf, at that time... Wasn't that the very same Dame Gertrude?

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: It was either her father–– or her oldest brother... I can't really remember, but it wasn't actually her.

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: Though the Graf at the time designated this area for the Infected, he didn't care whether the people in it lived or died. He even had all the industrial facilities torn down.

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: Obviously, to have us fend for ourselves.

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: So among the nobles, this place became known as 'the Afterglow,' and the concert hall also became the 'Afterglow Hall.'

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: The name, 'Afterglow,' represented the idea that we wouldn't last long, just like the last rays of light in the evening.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: That... That's simply cruel and unusual.

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: It was pretty over-the-top.

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: But for the Afterglow at the time, that word was a perfect fit.

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: Everyone fought desperately to survive, to let the lingering rays of sunlight on the horizon struggle for just a bit longer.

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: We set up stalls, we ran errands. Some of us even turned into hired thugs for rich people in the other plates... Hah, those were some chaotic years.

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: Later on, Herr Czerny stepped forward.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Stepped forward?

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: He started out as a nobody.

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: He had written a few pieces, but since he was an Infected, everything was published anonymously.

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: His works were magnificent, even attracting attention from the fancy folk atop the spires. But once they saw that Herr Czerny was from the Afterglow, they quickly turned away and left.

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: That was until he wrote 'Morgen und Abend.'

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: Ursula would be more qualified to speak about 'Morgen und Abend' than me, so I'll turn the floor over to her.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Ms. Ursula?

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: Oh, it's actually quite simple.

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: The one who taught piano to Mein Herr had a daughter, and she was good friends with him.

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: The two were on very good terms, and they were just about as good as each other. They were awfully competitive, always trying to one-up the other.

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: Sadly, the girl passed away when Mein Herr was twenty years old.

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: Losing her was a huge blow to him. Day in n' day out, he spoke hardly a word. He grew thinner and thinner by the day.

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: Until finally, he showed a stack of sheet music, told me it's his newest composition, and that he wasn't gonna publish anonymously this time.

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: The Gräfin then–– she was the very same Dame you mentioned.

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: Still don't know why, by the Gräfin sought out Mein Herr.

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: She became his sponsor, and also went 'long with all his ideas. She gave him her full backing, finally lettin' 'Morgen und Abend' carry the Czerny, and spread it all throughout the Afterglow.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I can't imagine that.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: But I'm starting to understand a bit of what Mr. Czerny meant in his saying...

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: 'Morgen und Abend' was so popular and beloved, the folk in the spires couldn't blind eye anymore. They had no choice, they had to acknowledge Mein Herr's talent.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: So then, Mr. Czerny began to cultivate people in the Afterglow who had musical talent?

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: That's right. Seeing as how we are in Leithanien, the one thing we aren't short on is musicians! I may not have any talent, but even I...

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: Oh stop it, you're just being humble.

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: A few years ago you were still playin' the accordion while yodelin' about your pickled cabbage.

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: Haha, back in my factory days, I had to gather everyone up for lunch. Way easier to use an accordion than to shout.

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: Anyway, once music became a part of the Afterglow, our worst days finally passed.

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: Composin', performin', teachin', makin' instruments...

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: Plenty of folk publish their compositions anonymously, and most performers can't leave the Afterglow. But still, the money it brought in gave the Afterglow a foot in the door.

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: But before long, Mein Herr got into some big fight with the Gräfin.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: A big fight?

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: Looked like a clash of ideas... not that understand such things.

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: The Gräfin stayed the Herr's patron, but the two have hardly made contact since.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Andante? What's wrong?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Kreide's grandfather... he's gone missing?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I'll head back right away!

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Thank you very much! See you!

steps.name: Tailor Store Owner
steps.text: Goodbye, hope to see you again! If anything doesn't fit quite right, bring it back and I'll fix it for you!

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: (It's already so late... Ebenholz should be back by now, right?)

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Huh, what is that...?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: An Originium slug?
